D6 - Mutation Testing (new)¶
This is a new individual deliverable.

What it is. A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (mutants), such as flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is killed. If all tests pass, the mutant survived: your tests did not notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.

What to do. For one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two such issues; your small issue may be one of them):

Run a mutation testing tool on the source files changed by your PR(s) for that issue. Do not run it on the whole project.
Using the tool's report, analyze every surviving mutant: is it equivalent (it behaves exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a gap in your tests? If there are more than 10 surviving mutants, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines your PR added or changed.
Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a surviving mutant that revealed a gap. Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no surviving mutant reveals a gap (all are killed or equivalent), say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
Answer the questions in the template below.
Evidence. Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (StrykerJS: add "json" to reporters; Gremlins: --output=<file>.json; go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file). Commit the report from your first run and from your re-run as docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json and -after.json (.txt for go-mutesting). The mutation scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.
</pasted_content id="1cf2">

docs/sprint3/mutation/97-tigerk9.md:**What was mutated.** The three source files the PR changes in `packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/export/`: `pdfText.ts` (new: cleans text so jsPDF's built-in font can draw it), `budgetMonthPdfRows.ts` (row shape: one Category column, separate Total and To Budget types) and `budgetMonthPdf.ts` (table layout, styles, "Page N of M"). The PR's only other source change is the one-line PDF title in `BudgetExportMenu.tsx`, a React component that the unit tests don't render, so I left it out. The tests run are the three PDF test files plus `budgetMonthCsv.test.ts`, which guards AC8 (the CSV export must not change).
docs/sprint3/mutation/97-tigerk9.md:- **Command runner, as in #163.** The Vitest runner (`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.0.0) runs no tests for any mutant with Vitest 5, so every mutant "survives". Bennett documented this in [125-bennettmatuszewski.md](125-bennettmatuszewski.md). I used his workaround: Stryker's command runner starts Vitest once per mutant (`--bail 1 --maxWorkers 1`).
docs/sprint3/mutation/97-tigerk9.md:- **Separate config files.** I added `stryker.issue-97.config.json` and `vitest.stryker.issue-97.config.mts` instead of editing Bennett's, so his command still reproduces his report.
docs/sprint3/mutation/97-tigerk9.md:  - `vitest.stryker.issue-97.setup.ts` initializes i18next. The regular test run initializes it indirectly (`setupTests.ts` → mocks → redux store → i18n). Without it, `t('Total')` returns `undefined` and 16 tests fail before Stryker starts. I checked that all 57 (before) and 73 (after) tests pass under this config before each run.
docs/sprint3/mutation/97-tigerk9.md:- **Commits.** [`33f7a49f6`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/33f7a49f6) is the code and tests the before run saw; [`08cd6fa9d`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/08cd6fa9d) adds the tests written from the survivor analysis, the after report and this write-up. I made the before run before committing anything, so to build `33f7a49f6` I took those tests back out. One difference: the "indents category names" test uses the version without `as` casts that I cleaned up later, which has the same assertions. I reran Stryker on `33f7a49f6` and got the same 75.15%, with every one of the 169 mutants in the same state as the before report.
docs/sprint3/mutation/97-tigerk9.md:- **Timeouts.** My first after run used `concurrency: 4`. It reported 4 mutants in `budgetMonthPdf.ts` (lines 114–117) as timed out, which Stryker counts as detected (92.90%). They had survived the before run, and two of them are equivalent (see the table), so the timeouts were the machine being overloaded, not tests catching them. I reran at `concurrency: 2` and they survived with no timeouts. The after report and score above are from that run, and the committed config uses 2. The before run had no timeouts at 4.

Run Stryker on **[packages/loot-core/src/server/attachments/app.ts](packages/loot-core/src/server/attachments/app.ts)**.

It isn't the biggest file by line count, but it's the best fit for this assignment. Here are the source files PR #175 changed (merge commit `482b82743`), largest first, with test files left out:

| File | Lines added |
|---|---|
| desktop-client/.../attachments/TransactionAttachmentsModal.tsx | 359 |
| desktop-client/.../attachments/AttachmentViewerModal.tsx | 299 |
| **loot-core/src/server/attachments/app.ts** | **290** |
| loot-core/src/shared/attachments.ts | 149 |
| loot-core/src/server/attachments/archive.ts | 109 |
| desktop-client/.../attachments/attachmentUtils.ts | 109 |
| loot-core/src/server/attachments/storage.ts | 97 |

**Why app.ts over the two bigger modals:**
- **It has the biggest unit test file in the PR.** `app.test.ts` adds 475 lines, so your score will reflect real tests rather than gaps in coverage.
- **It's plain server logic, not JSX.** A lot of the modal code is markup, styles and text labels. Stryker would mutate those strings and objects into many survivors you'd then have to explain as equivalent in your table.
- **It runs faster.** The modal tests render in a simulated browser, so each mutant takes much longer to test.
- **All 290 lines are new in your PR**, so you can pick any survivor for the "lines your PR added or changed" analysis.

**One setup difference:** your teammates' Stryker configs (Bennett's from #163, and the ones for #97 and #159) all live in `packages/desktop-client`. `app.ts` is in `packages/loot-core`, so you'll need a new config there. The same workaround still applies: the Vitest runner doesn't work with Vitest 5, so use Stryker's command runner (`--bail 1 --maxWorkers 1`), as described in [docs/sprint3/mutation/97-tigerk9.md](docs/sprint3/mutation/97-tigerk9.md).

The assignment says "the source files changed by your PR", so if you have time you could also mutate `storage.ts` and `archive.ts` in the same run. They're small, sit in the same package and each has its own test file.

// Vitest config for mutation testing the PDF export fixes (issue #97) with
// StrykerJS. stryker.issue-97.config.json runs it once per mutant.
//
// Based on Bennett Matuszewski's vitest.stryker.config.mts from #163: a
// standalone config rather than the full vite.config.mts, which copies
// public assets every time it loads and fails when Stryker's parallel
// workers load it at the same time. These unit tests only need module
// resolution.
//
// One addition: the shared row walk (budgetMonthRows.ts) imports
// MonthsContext.tsx, so JSX has to be compiled. The repo's tsconfig sets
// `jsx: preserve`, and without the React plugin nothing else compiles it.
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  oxc: { jsx: { runtime: 'automatic' } },
  resolve: {
    conditions: ['electron-renderer', 'module', 'browser', 'default'],
    tsconfigPaths: true,
  },
  test: {
    include: [
      'src/components/budget/export/pdfText.test.ts',
      'src/components/budget/export/budgetMonthPdfRows.test.ts',
      'src/components/budget/export/budgetMonthPdf.test.ts',
      // Guards AC8: the PDF changes must not change the CSV export.
      'src/components/budget/export/budgetMonthCsv.test.ts',
    ],
    environment: 'node',
    globals: true,
    setupFiles: ['./vitest.stryker.issue-97.setup.ts'],
  },
});

# Mutation testing: Issue #97 -- Improve PDF export formatting/data view

**PR(s):** #176  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.0.0 (command runner; see [Setup notes](#setup-notes))  **Config:** [`packages/desktop-client/stryker.issue-97.config.json`](../../../packages/desktop-client/stryker.issue-97.config.json), [`vitest.stryker.issue-97.config.mts`](../../../packages/desktop-client/vitest.stryker.issue-97.config.mts) and [`vitest.stryker.issue-97.setup.ts`](../../../packages/desktop-client/vitest.stryker.issue-97.setup.ts), based on Bennett Matuszewski's setup from #163  **Command:** `cd packages/desktop-client && npx stryker run stryker.issue-97.config.json`
**Reports:** [before](reports/97-tigerk9-before.json) · [after](reports/97-tigerk9-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 75.15% → after 90.53%

|        | Mutants | Killed | Timed out | Survived | Score  |
| ------ | ------- | ------ | --------- | -------- | ------ |
| Before | 169     | 127    | 0         | 42       | 75.15% |
| After  | 169     | 153    | 0         | 16       | 90.53% |

| File                    | Before  | After   |
| ----------------------- | ------- | ------- |
| `pdfText.ts`            | 85.71%  | 100.00% |
| `budgetMonthPdfRows.ts` | 100.00% | 100.00% |
| `budgetMonthPdf.ts`     | 59.26%  | 80.25%  |

**What was mutated.** The three source files the PR changes in `packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/export/`: `pdfText.ts` (new: cleans text so jsPDF's built-in font can draw it), `budgetMonthPdfRows.ts` (row shape: one Category column, separate Total and To Budget types) and `budgetMonthPdf.ts` (table layout, styles, "Page N of M"). The PR's only other source change is the one-line PDF title in `BudgetExportMenu.tsx`, a React component that the unit tests don't render, so I left it out. The tests run are the three PDF test files plus `budgetMonthCsv.test.ts`, which guards AC8 (the CSV export must not change).

## Setup notes

- **Command runner, as in #163.** The Vitest runner (`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.0.0) runs no tests for any mutant with Vitest 5, so every mutant "survives". Bennett documented this in [125-bennettmatuszewski.md](125-bennettmatuszewski.md). I used his workaround: Stryker's command runner starts Vitest once per mutant (`--bail 1 --maxWorkers 1`).
- **Separate config files.** I added `stryker.issue-97.config.json` and `vitest.stryker.issue-97.config.mts` instead of editing Bennett's, so his command still reproduces his report.
- **Two additions to the standalone Vitest config:**
  - The shared row walk (`budgetMonthRows.ts`) imports `MonthsContext.tsx`, so the config compiles JSX (`oxc: { jsx: { runtime: 'automatic' } }`). Without it, the CSV and row tests fail to load.
  - `vitest.stryker.issue-97.setup.ts` initializes i18next. The regular test run initializes it indirectly (`setupTests.ts` → mocks → redux store → i18n). Without it, `t('Total')` returns `undefined` and 16 tests fail before Stryker starts. I checked that all 57 (before) and 73 (after) tests pass under this config before each run.
- **Commits.** [`33f7a49f6`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/33f7a49f6) is the code and tests the before run saw; [`08cd6fa9d`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/08cd6fa9d) adds the tests written from the survivor analysis, the after report and this write-up. I made the before run before committing anything, so to build `33f7a49f6` I took those tests back out. One difference: the "indents category names" test uses the version without `as` casts that I cleaned up later, which has the same assertions. I reran Stryker on `33f7a49f6` and got the same 75.15%, with every one of the 169 mutants in the same state as the before report.
- **Timeouts.** My first after run used `concurrency: 4`. It reported 4 mutants in `budgetMonthPdf.ts` (lines 114–117) as timed out, which Stryker counts as detected (92.90%). They had survived the before run, and two of them are equivalent (see the table), so the timeouts were the machine being overloaded, not tests catching them. I reran at `concurrency: 2` and they survived with no timeouts. The after report and score above are from that run, and the committed config uses 2. The before run had no timeouts at 4.

## Surviving mutants

All 42 survivors are in lines this PR added. "Gap" = a test was missing; "Equivalent" = no test can tell the mutant from the original. "Killed by" names the test added after the before run (all in `src/components/budget/export/`).

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pdfText.ts:28 | `code === 0x200e \|\|` → `false` (×2) | Gap | The tests only used the two direction marks `useFormat` emits today (U+202A/U+202C). The issue's Design 1 lists U+200E too. Killed by `pdfText.test.ts › strips the direction mark U+%s`. |
| pdfText.ts:28 | `code === 0x200e \|\| code === 0x200f` → `&&` | Gap | Same gap as the row above. |
| pdfText.ts:29 | `code === 0x200f` → `false` | Gap | Same gap: U+200F was never tested. |

## Questions

**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**

My first tests checked what the PDF says but didn't say anything about where or how it says things. The text checks were already solid, `budgetMonthPdfRows.ts` was already at 100% and every amount-formatting mutant was killed. Several tests passed for the wrong reason though. The "never splits a row" check used one-line rows, which can't be on a page break to begin with. The page-number check found "Page 1 of 2" without checking what was actually on the page. The style test checked that the four row type differ, but not how, so dropping Total's border still passed because bold kept the rows different. The `pdfText.ts` survivors showed I had only tested the characters `useFormat` currently produces, not the full set the issue's design said to strip. I left the title and footer font gaps open on purpose, as no AC specifies fonts, and a test that pins jsPDF's internal font numbers would just be brittle.

**2. Did any survivor expose an assertion whose expected value wasn't based on the requirements?**

None of the assertions had a wrong expected value, though one test was weaker than its requirement. The AC7 test was named "repeats the header", but it only checked the "Budgeted" header, so any of the other three could have been blank. AC7 says the column header row repeats, so the fixed tests check all four header texts on every page. While writing tests the code formatter (lint) rewrote `’` into an ASCII `'` in both the input and the expected value of one of the tests. The test still passed while checking nothing about the apostrophe-dot format. I found it by scanning the files for non-ASCII characters and changed the tests to build the characters from code points.

**3. AI use, and what was verified or corrected.**

I used Claude (Opus 5.5) extensively in this. I used it to set up the Stryker config, run both passes, and draft the survivor table. My AI log can be found in my AI logs with the blurb "issue-97-pdf-export". I checked the classifications rather than taking them as Claude gave them. Each claim was confirmed with a small script against the real jsPDF/autotable that Claude would run (I would check results); default font size 16, 40pt margins, default cell styles, and Times as the fallback for an unknown font. There were 4 timeouts in the first run, which I ran again at lower concurrency, and this lowered the reported score from 92.90% to 90.53% as the tests survived instead of timing out.

Sprint 3: Project Development & Testing[¶](#sprint-3-project-development-testing "Permanent link")
==================================================================================================

**Nov 3 – Nov 19 · All deliverables due Nov 19, 11:59 PM (mid-sprint check-in due Nov 12) · 100 points (12% of course grade)**

Sprint 3 continues the development of your project and puts the focus on **testing**: how well your tests check what your code is supposed to do. The issue backlog, PR workflow, and general expectations carry forward; see [Sprint 1](../sprint1/) and [Sprint 2](../sprint2/) for anything not explicitly changed here. This page covers what is **new or different** in Sprint 3.

* * *

Sprint 3 at a glance

**Key dates:** Nov 12: check-in + at least one code PR (open or merged) · Nov 19: everything else

**Important rules (they cost the most points):**

*   No merge without an approval on the latest commit.
*   Spec review on the issue, saying what was checked.
*   Every code PR links its issue.
*   Real AI logs.
*   Test Evidence table in every PR; expected values not copied from the code's output.
*   Mutation testing with a tool, before and after reports committed.
*   Your team introduces no new test failures; skipped tests and disabled checks need an issue.

Unfamiliar with a term?

Check the [Glossary](../glossary/) for definitions of terms used throughout this page.

* * *

### Before you begin[¶](#before-you-begin "Permanent link")

*   **Check your AI log setup** against the [AI Log Instructions](../ai-logs/) before your first session.
*   **Read "Things that must improve"** below. These issues were observed in Sprint 2 and will be graded strictly.
*   **Record your baseline early** (see D8): the test results at your Sprint 2 release tag (`-csci435-s2`), from CI or by running the relevant test suites locally. It helps you find hardening issues and get the mutation tool running.
*   **Try the mutation testing tool early** (see D6), on any existing file in the part of the code you work on. Do not wait until your PRs are ready.

* * *

### What is new in Sprint 3[¶](#what-is-new-in-sprint-3 "Permanent link")

*   **Mutation testing** (D6): a new individual deliverable. It **replaces** the UML diagrams from Sprint 2.
*   **Test evidence section** in every PR description (D4).
*   **Hardening issues**: one of your issues may be a hardening issue (D1).
*   **Suite health section** in the sprint report (D8).
*   **Mid-sprint check-in requires an open PR** (D7), due Nov 12.

Team feature for Sprints 3–4

Each team will be assigned a larger feature that spans Sprints 3 and 4. The instructor or TA will post it as an issue in your team's issue tracker and notify your team when it is posted. You will likely need to split it into sub-issues.

* * *

### Things that must improve from Sprint 2[¶](#things-that-must-improve-from-sprint-2 "Permanent link")

These issues were observed in Sprint 2 and will be graded strictly in Sprint 3.

**1\. Open PRs early.** In Sprint 2, most PRs were opened in the last two days, which left no time for review. In Sprint 3, you need a code PR by the mid-sprint check-in (see D7).

**2\. Independent approval before merging.** A PR is merged only after a teammate approves its **latest commit**. Merging without an approval, or after pushing new commits since the approval, is not allowed. Once approved, the author may merge. To keep reviews moving, request the review on GitHub and notify your reviewer on Zulip; reviewers respond (approve or request changes) within 24 hours.

**3\. Spec reviews must be visible and show what was checked.** Before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment on the issue itself. The comment states what the reviewer checked: whether each acceptance criterion is clear and testable, which cases were considered (and whether they are covered), and whether the scope fits. If the reviewer finds problems, they list them and the author updates the spec. If the spec is good, the reviewer says so and approves, but "Looks good!" with nothing about what was checked is not acceptable.

**4\. Link PRs and issues.** Every code PR must link the issue it addresses, so the PR can be checked against the spec. Use `Closes #<issue>` in the PR description so the issue closes automatically when the PR is merged, and attach issues and code PRs to the `Sprint 3` milestone.

**5\. AI logs must be real logs.** A log shows your prompts and the AI's output (SpecStory format recommended; see the [AI Log Instructions](../ai-logs/)). The following are **not** logs and receive no full credit: summaries of a session, paraphrased prompts, a share link to a chat, or tool output without the prompts that produced it. File names must follow `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`. Link the log from the issue or PR it documents.

**6\. The sprint report must render.** Check that tables and links display correctly on GitHub (no escaped `\|` or `\[`). Use the Sprint 3 sections, not a copy of a previous report.

* * *

### Deliverables[¶](#deliverables "Permanent link")

#### D1 - Sprint Backlog[¶](#d1-sprint-backlog "Permanent link")

Same process as Sprint 2 ([D1](../sprint2/#d1-sprint-backlog)), including the priority on carryovers: unfinished Sprint 2 issues go into your Sprint 3 backlog first, or you document on the issue why they are dropped.

**Scope minimums for Sprint 3** (same as Sprint 2):

| Role | Minimum issues |

| Each CSCI 435 member | at least 2 medium issues (or equivalent story points) |
| Each CSCI 535 (grad) member | at least 2 medium issues + 1 additional small issue (or equivalent story points) |

**Scope must be justified.** Each issue states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences on why: which components it touches and how much change you expect. The instructor or TA may reclassify an issue whose scope is clearly overstated.

**Hardening issues (optional).** One of your issues may be a _hardening issue_: work that makes the existing system more reliable rather than adding a feature. Good sources:

*   **Your baseline run** (see D8): failing tests, flaky tests, or broken CI checks on `main`.
*   **Tech debt your team recorded** in the "Introduced" and "Encountered" fields of your Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 PRs.
*   **Known bugs** found in reviews, after merging, or by teammates.
*   **The upstream issue tracker**, for bugs in the parts of the system your team works on.

A hardening issue is scoped like any other issue (see the scope justification above). It must also include evidence that the problem is fixed:

*   **Bug fix:** a test that fails before the fix and passes after.
*   **Flaky test:** the root cause, and enough repeated runs of that test before and after the fix to show the change (for example, 20 runs for a unit test or 10 for an E2E test).
*   **Broken or missing CI check:** links to CI runs before and after the fix.
*   **Failing tests in the baseline:** pass/fail counts before and after, and the cause of each group of failures.

Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without fixing its cause counts as small at most.

**Team feature.** When the team feature issue is posted (see the box under "What is new in Sprint 3"), split it into sub-issues, each with its own owner, spec (D2), and scope. Link each sub-issue to the feature issue. Sub-issues count toward your scope minimum like any other issue. When the feature is posted, add its sub-issues to your Sprint 3 milestone and adjust your backlog as needed.

Create a `Sprint 3` milestone in GitHub and attach all selected issues to it.

**What to provide in D8 (Sprint report):** link to the Sprint 3 milestone and the rationale for your backlog decisions.

* * *

#### D2 - Requirements Specification[¶](#d2-requirements-specification "Permanent link")

Same format and requirements as Sprint 1 ([D2](../sprint1/#d2-requirements-specification)). Specs must be written and reviewed before coding begins; see item 3 in "Things that must improve" for what counts as a review.

Hardening issues use a bug format (include the observed and expected behaviors, the steps to reproduct the issue, and other details about the issue) when they fix a defect. Otherwise, use a short task format: the problem, the goal, acceptance criteria, and other necessary details.

* * *

#### D3 - Design Decisions[¶](#d3-design-decisions "Permanent link")

Same as Sprint 2 ([D3](../sprint2/#d3-design-decisions)): each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and explains the choice.

* * *

#### D4 - Code Changes and Pull Requests[¶](#d4-code-changes-and-pull-requests "Permanent link")

Same workflow as Sprint 2 ([D4](../sprint2/#d4-code-changes-and-pull-requests)), including **the Tech Debt section**. Sprint 3 adds a **Test Evidence** section to every PR description. It replaces the "how it was tested" part of the description, so you don't write it twice.

`## Test Evidence  | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value | |---|---|---|---| | AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |  **Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]  **AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]`

How to fill it in:

*   **One row per acceptance criterion** from D2. For bug reports, use the Expected Behavior instead. For PRs that change no product behavior (for example, CI changes), write "N/A" and explain why.
*   **Test(s):** the test name (and file, if not obvious). If you checked the AC manually, write `Manual:` followed by the steps and what you saw. If an AC is tested both automatically and manually, list both in the same row.
*   **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E`, or `manual`.
*   **Source of expected value:** where the expected result in your test comes from. Use one of: `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or `other` (explain). **The current output of your own code is not a valid source**; a test whose expected value was copied from what the code returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
*   **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually only.
*   You may use AI to draft this section, but you are responsible for checking that it is accurate.

Example:

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |

| AC1: An end date before the start date is rejected with an error | `outOfOffice.schema.test.ts` > rejects end before start | unit | AC |
| AC2: The away badge appears on the booking page during the out-of-office window | `booking-ooo.e2e.ts` > shows away badge in window | E2E | AC |
| AC3: The badge text is readable in dark mode | Manual: enabled dark mode, opened the booking page during the window → badge text is readable | manual | issue discussion |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** AC3 depends on visual contrast, which our test setup does not check.

**If your fork has no CI** that runs your tests, include in the PR description the command(s) you ran and a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).

**Reviewers** add one line to the code review rubric ([Sprint 1, D4](../sprint1/#d4-code-changes-and-pull-requests)):

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |

| Test evidence — does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? |  |  |

* * *

#### D5 - AI Logs[¶](#d5-ai-logs "Permanent link")

Same requirements as Sprint 1 ([D5](../sprint1/#d5-ai-logs)) and the [AI Log Instructions](../ai-logs/), with the enforcement described in item 5 of "Things that must improve."

**Log storage:** `ai-logs/sprint3/<your-github-username>/`

* * *

#### D6 - Mutation Testing _(new)_[¶](#d6-mutation-testing-new "Permanent link")

This is a new individual deliverable.

**What it is.** A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (_mutants_), such as flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is _killed_. If all tests pass, the mutant _survived_: your tests did not notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.

**What to do.** For **one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests** (CSCI 535: **two** such issues; your small issue may be one of them):

1.  Run a mutation testing tool on the **source files changed by your PR(s)** for that issue. Do not run it on the whole project.
2.  Using the tool's report, analyze every surviving mutant: is it _equivalent_ (it behaves exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a gap in your tests? If there are more than 10 surviving mutants, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines your PR added or changed.
3.  Add or strengthen **at least one test that kills a surviving mutant** that revealed a gap. Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no surviving mutant reveals a gap (all are killed or equivalent), say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
4.  **Answer the questions in the template below**.

**Evidence.** Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (StrykerJS: add `"json"` to `reporters`; Gremlins: `--output=<file>.json`; go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file). Commit the report from your first run and from your re-run as `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and `-after.json` (`.txt` for go-mutesting). The mutation scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.

**A tool is required.** Manual mutation does not count.

| Stack | Tool |

| TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest (Actual Budget, Cal.diy, Excalidraw, Outline, Gitea frontend) | [StrykerJS](https://stryker-mutator.io/) with the [Vitest runner](https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/stryker-js/vitest-runner/) |
| TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa) | [StrykerJS](https://stryker-mutator.io/) with the [Jest runner](https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/stryker-js/jest-runner/) |
| Go (Gitea backend) | [Gremlins](https://gremlins.dev/) or [go-mutesting](https://github.com/avito-tech/go-mutesting) |

**Set it up early.** Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is real work: builds, services, and choosing which tests run. Each student configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits the configuration they used. You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are encouraged to), as long as you run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.

**Common problems** to watch for:

*   **The tool stops before mutating.** Tools first run your tests on the unchanged code. If any of the selected tests fail, the run stops. Fix or exclude failing tests first (this is where your baseline run helps).
*   **Tests run against built code.** If your tests run against compiled output (for example, a `dist` folder) instead of the source, mutants in the source are never seen by the tests. Configure the tool to rebuild before testing, or choose tests that run on source.
*   **Tests need services.** Some test suites need a database or another service running. Start them before running the tool.
*   **False survivors.** If you limit which tests run (for example, with Vitest's `dir` option), make sure the tests that cover the mutated files are included. Otherwise, mutants that some test would catch are reported as survived or not covered. Before writing a new test for a survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
*   **Long runs.** Mutating only the files changed by your PR keeps run time manageable.

If you are blocked

If you cannot get the tool to run, first ask your teammates: someone may already have a working setup. If you are still stuck, tell the TA **as early as possible**, with the errors you got and the AI log of what you tried. The TA will help you debug it. If it still cannot be made to work, the TA may approve running the tool on a different issue or a different part of your code instead. Problems reported at the end of the sprint will not excuse a missing D6.

**Submission:** `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<username>.md`, using this template:

``# Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <issue title>  **PR(s):** #...  **Tool:** ...  **Config:** [link; credit the teammate if you reused their setup]  **Command:** `...` **Reports:** [before](reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json) · [after](reports/<issue#>-<username>-after.json) **Mutation score:** before ...% → after ...%  ## Surviving mutants  | Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why | |---|---|---|---| | | | | |  ## New or strengthened test  Commit: [link] · Test: [file > test name] · Kills: [mutant location]  ## Questions  1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests? 2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain. 3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct? If AI was not used, write "N/A."``

#### D8 - Sprint Report[¶](#d8-sprint-report "Permanent link")

Same format as Sprint 1 ([D6 in Sprint 1](../sprint1/#d6-sprint-report)), with these additions:

*   **Suite health** (new section). Keep it short:
    *   **Baseline table** for the test suites relevant to your team (the packages or areas you work on, not the whole repository). For each suite: the command or CI workflow, and the test runner's summary line (passed, failed, skipped) at your **Sprint 2 release tag** (`-csci435-s2`) and at the **end** of the sprint. Use CI results where available; if you run tests locally, run only the packages you change.
    *   **Failures grouped by cause** (for example: environment-specific, already broken upstream, flaky, caused by our changes), with a link to one issue per cause that lists the affected tests.
    *   **No failures introduced by your team.** Any test your team's changes broke must be fixed by the end of the sprint. Pre-existing failures only need to be recorded and grouped; fixing them is optional (and can be a hardening issue).
    *   **Skipped tests and disabled CI checks.** Skipping a test or disabling a CI check requires a linked issue and a reason in a code comment.
*   **Mutation testing:** links to each member's D6 file.
*   **Hardening issues:** which issues they are and where they came from.

### Grading[¶](#grading "Permanent link")

Sprint 3 is worth **100 points** (12% of the course grade). D1, D8, and D9 are graded as a team; all other deliverables are graded individually.

| Deliverable | Points | Notes |

| D1 - Sprint Backlog | 10 | Team. Issues selected, scoped with justification, assigned, milestone created; carryover decisions documented |
| D2 - Requirements Specification | 20 | Individual. User story format, INVEST criteria, acceptance criteria quality; spec review on the issue before coding, showing what was checked |
| D3 - Design Decisions | 5 | Individual. At least one non-trivial decision per issue, with alternatives |
| D4 - Pull Requests | 20 | Individual. See detail below |
| D5 - AI Logs | 5 | Individual. Real logs, correctly named, linked from the issue or PR |
| D6 - Mutation Testing | 15 | Individual. See rubric below |
| D7 - Mid-Sprint Check-in | 5 | Individual. On time, substantive, and an open or merged code PR linked = 5; late, thin, or no PR = 3; missing = 0 |
| D8 - Sprint Report | 10 | Team. Completeness, specificity, quality of evidence; suite health section |
| D9 - Sprint Release | 2 | Team. Tag follows convention; created after the last merge; release description summarizes changes |
| D10 - Reflection Survey | 8 | Individual. Required for completion |
| **Total** | **100** |  |

**D4 - PR grading detail:**

The D4 score is the aggregate across all your PRs, normalized to 20 points.

| Criterion | Points per PR |

| Change correctly implements the acceptance criteria from D2 | 6 |
| Tests written or updated appropriately; Test Evidence section complete, with every AC covered and expected values justified | 6 |
| PR description explains what changed and why; Tech Debt section present; issue linked | 3 |
| CI passes (or manual verification documented) | 3 |
| Code reviewed using the rubric (including the test evidence line); reviewer comment posted; PR merged only after an approval on the latest commit | 2 |
| **Total per PR** | **20** |

**D6 - Mutation testing rubric:**

| Criterion | Points |

| Tool run on the files changed by the PR; configuration, command, results, and reports committed | 4 |
| Surviving mutants analyzed correctly (equivalent vs. test gap, with explanation) | 4 |
| At least one new or strengthened test kills a surviving mutant; re-run confirms it | 4 |
| Answers to the questions show understanding, not just description | 3 |
| **Total** | **15** |

CSCI 535: the D6 score is the average of the two submissions.

Minimum bar

A team with no merged PRs (D4), no sprint report (D8), or no release (D9) receives a **0 for Sprint 3** regardless of other deliverables.

Extra credit

*   A PR submitted to the **real upstream project** and accepted or under active review earns up to **3 bonus points** per PR, at the instructor's discretion.
*   A **bug report filed in the upstream project** that comes from your own testing work and is **confirmed by the maintainers** (by the time Sprint 4 is graded) earns up to **2 bonus points** per report, at the instructor's discretion.

// Vitest config for mutation testing the transaction attachments UI from
// issue #154 (PR #175) with StrykerJS. stryker.issue-154.config.json runs
// it once per mutant.
//
// Based on Bennett Matuszewski's vitest.stryker.config.mts from #163: a
// standalone config rather than the full vite.config.mts, which copies
// public assets every time it loads and fails when Stryker's parallel
// workers load it at the same time. Unlike #163's tests, these render React
// components, so this keeps the parts of vite.config.mts that the regular
// component test run uses: the React plugin, the build-shims injection,
// jsdom and src/setupTests.ts. The React Compiler (babel) plugin is left out;
// it only adds memoization, and the tests pass without it.
import * as path from 'path';

import inject from '@rollup/plugin-inject';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import type { Plugin } from 'vite';
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

const injectShims = {
  enforce: 'post',
  apply: 'serve',
  ...(inject({
    exclude: ['src/setupTests.ts'],
    global: [path.resolve('./src/build-shims.js'), 'global'],
  }) as unknown as Plugin),
} satisfies Plugin;

export default defineConfig({
  resolve: {
    conditions: ['electron-renderer', 'module', 'browser', 'default'],
    tsconfigPaths: true,
  },
  plugins: [injectShims, react()],
  test: {
    include: [
      'src/components/attachments/TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx',
      'src/components/attachments/AttachmentViewerModal.test.tsx',
      // The paperclip column and useTransactionAttachmentCounts
      'src/components/transactions/TransactionsTable.test.tsx',
    ],
    environment: 'jsdom',
    globals: true,
    setupFiles: './src/setupTests.ts',
    testTimeout: 10000,
    onConsoleLog(_log: string, type: 'stdout' | 'stderr'): boolean | void {
      return type === 'stderr';
    },
  },
});

```

```mjs
// Merges the three StrykerJS JSON reports for issue #154 (PR #175) into the
// single report D6 asks for, and prints the mutation scores.
//
// PR #175 changed code in two packages, and the desktop-client code is run
// as two Stryker runs (modals, and the TransactionsTable paperclip column),
// so there are three reports:
//   packages/loot-core/reports/mutation/issue-154.json
//   packages/desktop-client/reports/mutation/issue-154.json
//   packages/desktop-client/reports/mutation/issue-154-table.json
//
// Usage (from the repo root):
//   node docs/sprint3/mutation/154-merge-reports.mjs <out.json> [loot-core.json desktop.json table.json]
//
// File paths are made relative to the repo root, and mutant ids get the
// run's name as a prefix, since every run numbers its mutants from 0.
// Nothing else in the mutant results is changed.
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import * as path from 'node:path';

const [out, ...inputs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!out) {
  console.error('usage: 154-merge-reports.mjs <out.json> [inputs...]');
  process.exit(1);
}

const runs = [
  {
    name: 'loot-core',
    dir: 'packages/loot-core',
    file: inputs[0] ?? 'packages/loot-core/reports/mutation/issue-154.json',
  },
  {
    name: 'desktop-client',
    dir: 'packages/desktop-client',
    file:
      inputs[1] ?? 'packages/desktop-client/reports/mutation/issue-154.json',
  },
  {
    name: 'desktop-client-table',
    dir: 'packages/desktop-client',
    file:
      inputs[2] ??
      'packages/desktop-client/reports/mutation/issue-154-table.json',
  },
];

const merged = {
  schemaVersion: '1',
  thresholds: { high: 80, low: 60 },
  projectRoot: '.',
  files: {},
  config: {},
};

for (const run of runs) {
  const report = JSON.parse(readFileSync(run.file, 'utf8'));
  merged.thresholds = report.thresholds ?? merged.thresholds;
  merged.framework ??= report.framework;
  merged.config[run.name] = report.config;
  for (const [file, result] of Object.entries(report.files)) {
    const rel = path.isAbsolute(file)
      ? path.relative(process.cwd(), file)
      : path.join(run.dir, file);
    merged.files[rel] = {
      ...result,
      mutants: result.mutants.map(m => ({
        ...m,
        id: `${run.name}:${m.id}`,
      })),
    };
  }
}

writeFileSync(out, JSON.stringify(merged));

// Stryker's mutation score: detected (killed + timed out) / valid mutants
// (everything except compile and runtime errors and ignored mutants).
function tally(mutants) {
  const t = { total: 0, killed: 0, timeout: 0, survived: 0, noCoverage: 0 };
  for (const m of mutants) {
    if (['CompileError', 'RuntimeError', 'Ignored'].includes(m.status)) {
      continue;
    }
    t.total++;
    if (m.status === 'Killed') t.killed++;
    else if (m.status === 'Timeout') t.timeout++;
    else if (m.status === 'Survived') t.survived++;
    else if (m.status === 'NoCoverage') t.noCoverage++;
  }
  t.score = ((100 * (t.killed + t.timeout)) / t.total).toFixed(2);
  return t;
}

const rows = Object.entries(merged.files).map(([file, r]) => [
  file,
  tally(r.mutants),
]);
rows.push(['ALL', tally(Object.values(merged.files).flatMap(r => r.mutants))]);

      `killed ${t.killed}  timeout ${t.timeout}  survived ${t.survived}  ` +
      `noCoverage ${t.noCoverage}  ${file}`,
  );
}

});

292	// Moves the live attachments of one transaction to another, for merges: the
293	// kept transaction ends up with the attachments of both. Removed attachments

295	//
296	// Undoing the merge brings the dropped transaction back but leaves the

299	export async function moveAttachments(
300	  fromTransactionId: TransactionAttachmentEntity['transaction_id'],
301	  toTransactionId: TransactionAttachmentEntity['transaction_id'],
302	) {
303	  // A split child's attachments go on its parent. A child never owns
304	  // attachments itself, so `fromTransactionId` needs no such step.
305	  const ownerId = await resolveOwnerTransactionId(toTransactionId);
306	  if (ownerId == null || ownerId === fromTransactionId) {
307	    return;
308	  }
309	
310	  const { changes } = db.runQuery(
311	    `UPDATE transaction_attachments SET transaction_id = ?
312	       WHERE transaction_id = ? AND tombstone = 0`,
313	    [ownerId, fromTransactionId],
314	  );
315	  if (Number(changes) > 0) {

333	// Attachments belong to non-child transactions: a split child's attachments
334	// go on its parent. Returns null if the transaction (or the child's parent)
335	// doesn't exist or is deleted.
336	async function resolveOwnerTransactionId(
337	  transactionId: string,
338	): Promise<string | null> {
339	  type Row = Pick<DbTransaction, 'id' | 'isChild' | 'parent_id' | 'tombstone'>;
340	  const query =
341	    'SELECT id, isChild, parent_id, tombstone FROM transactions WHERE id = ?';
342	
343	  const transaction = await db.first<Row>(query, [transactionId]);
344	  if (transaction == null || transaction.tombstone) {
345	    return null;
346	  }
347	  if (!transaction.isChild) {
348	    return transaction.id;
349	  }
350	  if (transaction.parent_id == null) {
351	    return null;
352	  }
353	
354	  const parent = await db.first<Row>(query, [transaction.parent_id]);
355	  if (parent == null || parent.tombstone) {
356	    return null;
357	  }
358	  return parent.id;
359	}
360	
361	function fromDbRow(row: DbTransactionAttachment): TransactionAttachmentEntity {
362	  return {
363	    id: row.id,
364	    transaction_id: row.transaction_id,
365	    file_name: row.file_name,
366	    // This app only writes validated types, but an imported budget could hold
367	    // anything; `attachment-read` reports the type found in the file instead
368	    mime_type: row.mime_type as AttachmentMimeType,
369	    size: row.size,
370	    storage: 'local',
371	    created_at: row.created_at,
372	    deleted_at: row.deleted_at,
373	    tombstone: row.tombstone === 1,
374	  };
375	}
376	
377	function notifyChanged() {
378	  connection.send('sync-event', {
379	    type: 'applied',
380	    tables: ['transaction_attachments'],
381	  });
382	}
383	
384	function reportError(message: string, error: unknown) {
385	  logger.error(message, error);
386	  if (error instanceof Error) {
387	    captureException(error);
388	  }
389	}
390

Issue #154 (CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget, sub-issue of #150) was rescoped on 2026-11-13 to store attachment files on the user's device only. It was implemented and merged as PR #175 (branch feat/attach-receipts) by 2026-11-16. The plan is at `/Users/james/ActualBudget/issue-154-plan.md` (outside the git repo).

**Why:** Server storage was about 35–40% of the original scope. #155 (mobile, delete/undo, cleanup) and #156 (find/export) don't build it. As of 2026-11-16 the #155 body refers to the server-storage issue as "#NEW", so it still hadn't been filed.

**How to apply:** Key facts from the merged design, which matter for #155:
- Rows are written with `db.runQuery` (no sync messages), so the app's undo stack can't see attachment changes.
- `transactionAttachmentCountsQuery` doesn't filter out deleted transactions.
- Files are stored at `<budgetDir>/attachments/<id>`, so `delete-budget` already removes them.
- Known gaps listed in the PR: re-downloading the budget drops the rows but leaves the files; `duplicate-budget` and backups don't copy attachments.
- Phase 0 decisions: attachments go on the parent transaction only; 10 MB limit; JPEG/PNG/WebP/PDF only.

See [[issue-155-scope]] if it is written later.

It is the source file in PR #175 with the most tests: `app.test.ts` has 38 of them, twice as many as any other test file in the PR. The tests run against each mutant are every test file that imports `app.ts`: `app.test.ts`, `archive.test.ts` (export and import) and `cleanup.test.ts`.

## Setup notes

- **Command runner, as in #163.** The Vitest runner (`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.0.0) runs no tests for any mutant with Vitest 5, so every mutant "survives". Bennett documented this in [125-bennettmatuszewski.md](125-bennettmatuszewski.md). I used his workaround: Stryker's command runner starts Vitest once per mutant (`--bail 1 --maxWorkers 1`).
- **Vitest config.** `vitest.stryker.issue-154.config.mts` reuses loot-core's own `vitest.config.ts` (setup file, resolve conditions) and only narrows `include` to the three test files above. I included `archive.test.ts` and `cleanup.test.ts` as well as `app.test.ts` because they call `app.ts`'s handlers too; leaving them out could have reported mutants they kill as survivors.
- **Same config for both runs.** The before run used the tests on `master`; the after run is the same command after adding the tests below. `app.ts` itself did not change between the runs. Neither run had timeouts (`concurrency: 3`).
